subject: Audit evidence extraction & staging playbook (preservation + handoff)
messages:
From: John Mercer <john.mercer@harborcorp.com>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Cc: harborcorp-compliance-team@harborcorp.com
Date: Tue, 2 Dec 2025 09:14:12 -0800
Subject: Request: Evidence extraction + staging plan and timelines

Evelyn —

Thanks for taking our RFP question on short notice. For HarborCorp's upcoming compliance window we need a concrete runbook for: full audit-trail extraction, redaction options for PII, a staging approach for multi-terabyte handoffs (S3-compatible), and tamper-evidence checks we can validate on receipt. Key constraints:
- We may request incremental snapshots (daily deltas) for a 90-day lookback, plus a one-time full-harvest for the prior 3 years.
- Export must be encrypted at rest in transit; HarborCorp will provide an S3 target with a dedicated bucket and IAM role, or we can accept a presigned URL-based push.
- Chain-of-custody manifest is required (checksums + file-level timestamps).

Can you provide a playbook that includes timelines for a full harvest (estimate TB/hour), how you handle redaction and sampling proof, and what evidence we will get back (manifests, checksums, logs)? Also include any temporary retention you require on your side and recommended retention policies on the staging bucket.

Appreciate a short (1-2 page) runbook and sample manifest we can attach to our procurement packet.

Regards,
John Mercer
Director, Compliance Operations
HarborCorp

---
Attachments: none
From: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
To: John Mercer <john.mercer@harborcorp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 3 Dec 2025 11:02:05 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Evidence extraction + staging plan and timelines

John —

Thanks for the clear ask. I attached a short playbook (redwood_evidence_playbook_v1.pdf) and a sample manifest (s3-handoff-manifest.csv) that map to your procurement checklist. Summary of the proposed approach here: 

1) Scope and cadence
- One-time full-harvest: we estimate ~1.2 TB/hour sustained for your current workload profile; final throughput will depend on snapshot compression and parallelism on the export host.
- Incremental/delta snapshots: configurable daily or hourly. Deltas are generated from the immutable event ledger and include offsets for replayability.

2) Redaction and sampling proof
- Redaction options: field-level redaction (PII tokenization), record-filtering (exclude by type), or encrypted blobs for customer-side redaction. We produce a redaction log showing which record IDs were altered.
- Proof: we include a pre/post-harvest sampling report with original/hashed values and a signed summary (SHA-256) of sampled rows to validate redaction integrity.

3) Transfer and staging
- Preferred: customer-provided S3 bucket + cross-account role with PutObject permissions. Alternative: presigned PUT URLs.
- Files uploaded as compressed NDJSON partitions (~100–500 MB each) with an accompanying manifest. Each file includes a per-file SHA256 and an overall tarball manifest for quick validation.
- We set object-lock retention for the staging prefix for 72 hours by default (can be extended per procurement).

4) Tamper evidence and chain-of-custody
- Each file: SHA-256 checksum, upload timestamp, uploader identity (service account ID), and transfer log.
- Delivery package: manifest CSV, signed manifest hash (PKCS7 signature), and a transfer audit log (line-level).

5) Timeline and scheduling
- Kickoff -> readiness checklist (2 business days)
- Full-harvest dry run (small slice) -> 1–2 business days
- Full harvest execution: estimated 48–72 hours for first full-run for ~80 TB, plus validation time.

6) Retention and on-redwood staging policy
- Default staging retention: 7 days post-delivery; can be configured to 0 days (zero retention) if HarborCorp prefers immediate purge after successful transfer.
- Retention on customer bucket: recommend 90-day hold for incremental runs and longer for archival copies; include lifecycle rules to move to Glacier if desired.

Next steps: please confirm whether you'll provide an IAM role or prefer presigned URLs. If IAM role, we'll share a minimal trust policy and the recommended prefix structure. If you want us to redact PII, mark the fields in the attached manifest and we'll include the redaction log in the delivery package.

I'll loop Marissa and Kimberly for execution-specific items (S3 config, runbook execution).

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Security
Redwood Inference

---

Marissa —

We can provision the export window using two additional export clusters behind the scheduler and request temporary egress bandwidth increase with finance. Quick notes: 
- Ephemeral signing: we'll generate a one-use RSA keypair per-harvest and publish the public key in the manifest; security will rotate keys and retain the private key in KMS for 30 days for traceability.
- Redaction pipeline: tokenization library is ready; we will output a redaction audit file (redaction_log.ndjson) that maps record_id -> redaction_type -> redaction_hash.
- Staging retention: by default we keep 7 days; we can support immediate purge after transfer completion but need the customer to accept responsibility for re-requesting data if required.

I'll draft the ops runbook addendum (S3 prefix naming, IAM role trust policy snippet, pre-signed URL expiry defaults) and attach a sample checksum file (egress-checksum-samples.txt) to the outgoing package. Marissa — once you confirm the final SLA window I can send the readiness checklist and proposed cluster schedule.

Kimberly Park
Principal Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
